previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for post-procedural monitoring and pain management following a flexible bronchoscopy with balloon dilation of the trachea and left main stem bronchus due to recurrent airway stenosis from relapsing polychondritis and Ruvalcaba-Myhre-Smith syndrome. The procedure successfully dilated the airways and removed obstructive pseudomembrane and granulation tissue. He experienced moderate chest pain managed with oxycodone and reported epigastric pain attributed to pirfenidone, which was addressed by increasing famotidine to twice daily. His white blood cell count rose post-procedure but was deemed reactive. He remained stable, with mild atelectasis on chest X-ray resolving clinically. He was discharged home with a short course of prednisone, instructions to continue all home medications, and follow-up planned with pulmonology.
problems: Long term (current) use of systemic steroids

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Mr ___,

It was a pleasure taking care of you at ___. 

Why was I here? 
- You were having difficulty breathing and your oxygen level was 
low. 

What was done for me while I was here?
- You were given medications (nebulizers) and extra oxygen 
(trach mask) to help you breathe. You also had a camera put in 
your breathing tube into your lungs (bronchoscopy), and the 
closed off tubes were opened up again (balloon dilation). 

What should I do when I go home?
- You should take your medications as prescribed to you, 
including the antibiotics that you breathe in (nebulized 
tobramycin). You should go to all your follow up appointments. 
You should call your doctor or go to the ED if you are having 
trouble breathing again. 

We wish you the best in the future. 
Sincerely, 
Your ___ care team
